title: LANsurfer monitoring
description: Operational health, HTTP latency/errors, pgx pool pressure, Go runtime and durable Game Request outcomes. One job/instance at a time; no PII or credentials.

panels.title: Scrape
panels.description: Scrape success only; failure may be process/network failure or an invalid Metrics API Key. Check SQL collection separately.

panels.title: SQL sources
panels.description: Each optional SQL source reports independently. A successful scrape with a failed source omits that source's product metrics.

panels.title: Pool in use
panels.description: Acquired connections / configured maximum. 80% and 95% are examples; investigate sustained saturation with waits or cancellations.

panels.title: Active requests
panels.description: Current open + playing requests, not completed games.

panels.title: Users
panels.description: Current registered users; decreases after account deletion.

panels.title: Uptime
panels.description: Resets on process restart; durable product totals do not.

panels.title: Application request rate
panels.description: Completed HTTP requests by exact response status. Excludes monitoring endpoints, assets/media, and long-lived SSE.

panels.title: Application 5xx fraction
panels.description: Server errors / completed application requests. No requests means no useful ratio; absent 5xx is zero only when denominator data exists.

panels.title: Application latency
panels.description: Histogram percentiles for completed requests. Excludes monitoring endpoints, assets/media and SSE stream lifetime. Sparse traffic makes percentiles unstable.

panels.title: Slowest route templates (p95)
panels.description: Five slowest route/method combinations at each sample; membership may change. Fixed chi route templates, never raw IDs or URLs.

targets.expr: topk(5, histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, method, route) (rate(lansurfer_http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="$job",instance="$instance",route!~"/metrics|/healthz|/readyz|/events/game-requests|/assets/.*|/media/.*"}[$__rate_interval]))))

panels.title: In-flight HTTP requests
panels.description: All active requests, including long-lived SSE and the scrape itself. Open streams are expected, not blocked page requests.

panels.title: Pool connections
panels.description: Acquired + idle + constructing make up total connections. Maximum is configuration, not the PostgreSQL server-wide limit. Lines are not stacked.

panels.title: Mean connection acquire / wait time
panels.description: Acquire duration / successful acquisitions; empty-acquire wait duration / waiting acquisitions. Means, not percentiles. Zero wait rate gives zero mean wait.

panels.title: Pool acquisition and churn rates
panels.description: Process-local rates. Waits/cancellations indicate pressure; connection churn may indicate lifetime/idle limits or instability.

panels.title: CPU usage (cores)
panels.description: CPU seconds per wall second. One means one fully used core; can exceed one on a multicore process.

panels.title: Memory
panels.description: Resident memory versus Go heap allocations. RSS includes more than the Go heap.

panels.title: Goroutines and OS threads
panels.description: Process-local counts; watch sustained growth rather than treating a single value as a leak.

panels.title: File descriptor utilization
panels.description: Linux open descriptors / process limit. Includes sockets/SSE and database connections. Unsupported platforms remain No data.

panels.title: Current Game Requests
panels.description: Open requests are forming; playing requests have explicitly started. Current-state gauges, not cumulative outcomes.

panels.title: Users, browser sessions and follows
panels.description: Unexpired sessions are not online users. Follows count relationships, not unique Games or players.

panels.title: Game Request event rates
panels.description: Sampled counter rates, not exact selected-period counts. Host auto-membership is not a join; first explicit open -> playing counts as started.

panels.title: Durable cumulative totals (not selected-period counts)
panels.description: Latest PostgreSQL-backed totals for one instance. Survive restarts/deletion. Historical upgrades are lower bounds; restores can reduce totals. Do not sum replicas sharing a database.
